jobs.title: Paid Student Internship w/Office of Diversity & Inclusion at New York State Office of the Attorney General
jobs.description: Employer: New York State Office of the Attorney General Expires: 11/13/2026 Administrative DivisionOffice of Diversity and Inclusion—New York CityStudent Assistant for Diversity, Equity, and InclusionReference No. ODI_NYC_PUGS_2026_2 Paid Part-Time Placements for Graduate and Undergraduate Students | Application Deadline is November 13, 2026*The Office of the New York State Attorney General’s (OAG) Office of Diversity and Inclusion (ODI) is seeking talented graduate and undergraduate students for a paid placement during the winter and spring terms. The mission of ODI is to provide leadership, guidance, and support with respect to diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) issues at OAG. Specific areas of focus include OAG policies and procedures, recruitment and hiring, staff education and training, employee engagement, procurement, and diversity and inclusion events. ODI supports OAG in building a diverse team and workplace that celebrates diversity and fosters a culture of inclusion, equity, and accessibility. Applicants must be available to start in November or by early to mid-December at the latest. Duties:Provide administrative support to the ODI, e.g., monitoring email and telephone calls;Assist with review of OAG policies through a DEIA lens to ensure alignment with industry standards and ODI mission;Assist with creating, analyzing, and interpreting survey data to identify trends and support ODI’s strategic initiatives;Research creative content for DEIA intranet, workshops, panel discussions, multicultural observances, and initiatives;Ability to review quantitative and qualitative survey data, identify key themes and trends, and translate findings into clear, plain-language insights;Conduct other internet research projects;Review DEIA trainings;Update catalog of trainings; Design event flyers; andAssist with special projects as needed. Please be advised ODI supports the operations of OAG and does not engage in legal casework. Qualifications:Demonstrates a highly professional attitude with the mindset of providing prompt and courteous customer service;Excellent written and verbal communication skills;Strong analytical skills;Able to work independently;Highly organized and detail oriented;Able to manage and prioritize multiple, time-sensitive tasks simultaneously;Proficient in Word, Excel, Forms, and Outlook;Prior experience with Canva or similar graphic design programs is preferred but not required; andForeign language proficiency is desirable. Placement DetailsThe format of this placement is hybrid. Students report to their designated workstation at 28 Liberty Street in Lower Manhattan two or three (2-3)days per week. On the days students work remotely, they need a reliable computer, a secure internet connection, a phone, and a sufficiently quiet and private workspace to telework.At the time students receive and accept a paid placement offer, they must provide written documentation demonstrating theyare full-time students in good academic standing as defined by their schools. Applications from students who are starting college/university during the 2026-27 academic year will not be considered.Applicants must be available to work 15-30 hours per week during regular business hours for at least the winter/spring term (November/December through May). Students who are available to continue working during the 2027 summer term are strongly preferred. Please be advised that reappointment for additional semesters/terms is possible but neither automatic nor guaranteed. The students hired for this placement will be hired as student assistants. Graduate students are paid the hourly rate of $20.25 and undergraduate students are paid the hourly rate of $18.55.*Applications are accepted online until November 13, 2026, and paid placement offers are made on a rolling basis.United States (U.S.) citizenship and New York state residency are not required, but applicants must be eligible to be employed in the U.S. Candidates from diverse backgrounds are encouraged to apply. The OAG is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to workplace diversity. How to ApplyThe following section provides detailed information about the application process and application requirements. Please review the complete list of instructions prior to preparing and submitting your application materials online. You will be unable to edit or amend your application after it has been submitted.Applications for paid student placements must be submitted online. To apply, please click the following link: www.ag.ny.gov/job-postings/undergraduate-graduate-studentsApplications are submitted separately for each bureau/regional office, and an applicant’s candidacy for each application is determined separately by each bureau/regional office.*Applications are accepted online until November 13, 2026, and placement offers are made on a rolling basis.The following four (4) documents must be submitted with your application: Your documents should reflect your own thoughts/work product in text that was written by you. Do not use artificial intelligence (AI) to generate application documents. Once submitted, you will not be able to access or edit your application. Therefore, we strongly encourage you to have someone review/proofread your documents ahead of submitting your application online. Cover Letter You may choose to address your letter to the Legal Recruitment Unit.Indicate why you are interested in a placement with OAG and what makes you a strong candidate.You may wish to include information about what life experiences you will bring to the position that will enhance OAG’s ability to better serve the diverse population of this state.ResumeEnsure your resume is complete and current prior to submitting your application.Reference ListSubmit a list of three (3) professional references (i.e., supervisor or professor).For each reference, indicate the nature and duration of your relationship.Include contact information and email addresses for each reference.Please note that your references will not be contacted until after you interview for the placement.Writing SampleSubmit a paper completed for school or a writing sample that was prepared for a job or during an internship/externship.Submit a sample that demonstrates your ability to analyze and organize information into an effective document.We recommend submitting a sample that is 2-4 pages in length.If needed, please include a cover page providing the reviewer with any relevant background information or context. Failure to submit a complete application will delay the consideration of your candidacy.If a bureau wishes to schedule an interview, they will contact you directly to arrange this meeting.The OAG provides reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities. If you have questions regarding a position with OAG, the application process, or need assistance with submitting your application, please contact Legal Recruitment via email at recruitment@ag.ny.gov or phone at 212-416-8080. For more information about OAG, please visit our website: ag.ny.gov

jobs.description: Employer: Concrete Strategies Expires: 11/13/2026 Quality Control InternCONCRETE STRATEGIES - Nationwide, USA, United StatesTagged: InternshipAs a Quality Control Intern at Concrete Strategies, you'll be at the forefront of maintaining the highest standards of construction quality and ensuring that our projects meet or exceed industry benchmarks. Your internship will offer hands-on experience in quality control processes, inspection procedures, and contributing to the delivery of exceptional construction outcomes.During your internship, you'll have the opportunity to learn about and contribute to:Quality Inspections: Participate in thorough quality inspections of construction materials, workmanship, and installations, ensuring compliance with specifications and industry standards.Documentation: Assist in maintaining accurate records of quality inspections, test results, and other relevant documentation to support the quality assurance process.Quality Assurance Plans: Learn to develop and implement quality assurance plans for construction projects, outlining processes and criteria to achieve desired quality levels.Collaboration: Work closely with project teams, subcontractors, and other stakeholders to address quality-related concerns and facilitate effective communication.Problem Solving: Engage in identifying quality issues, troubleshooting discrepancies, and contributing to solutions that align with project requirements.Testing and Analysis: Gain insights into performing tests and analyses on construction materials, such as concrete strength tests and structural assessments, to ensure they meet specified standards.Process Improvement: Contribute to continuous improvement efforts by suggesting enhancements to quality control procedures, practices, and workflows.Quality Training: Participate in training sessions focused on quality control methods, techniques, and tools used within the construction industry.Quality Compliance: Assist in ensuring that all construction activities adhere to regulatory requirements, codes, and standards.Professional Development: Engage in learning opportunities to enhance your knowledge of quality assurance principles and their practical application in construction.Concrete Strategies places a strong emphasis on delivering projects of the highest quality. As a QA/QC Intern, you'll be an integral part of upholding this commitment, helping to create structures that are not only safe but also built to last. This internship experience will provide you with valuable skills and insights that are valuable in pursuing a career in quality assurance and quality control within the construction field.QualificationsCurrently pursuing a degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Quality Assurance, or a related field.Interest in understanding and maintaining quality standards in construction projects.Familiarity with construction methods, materials, and quality control processes.Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications for data management and reporting.Keen eye for detail to identify discrepancies and deviations from quality standards.Ability to analyze project documentation, test results, and inspection reports.Effective verbal and written communication skills for collaboration with project teams and stakeholders.Willingness to address quality-related issues and contribute to solutions.Collaborative attitude, capable of working closely with quality control teams and project personnel.Strong organizational skills to maintain accurate records of quality assurance activities.Openness to adapting to changing project conditions and quality requirements.Eagerness to learn about quality control processes, industry standards, and best practices.About Concrete StrategiesConcrete Strategies is the nation’s leading full-service, design-build, turnkey concrete contractor. The firm has an unparalleled track record in architectural site cast concrete, structural concrete, flatwork, tilt-up and all types of self-perform concrete construction for commercial and industrial projects. Concrete Strategies employs over 1,000 field and office personnel and completes over $500 million in revenue annually performing work across the United States. As we continue to grow and expand our operations, we are continuously seeking talented individuals to join our team and contribute to our success.At Concrete Strategies, LLC, we are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace. We provide equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or veteran status. We believe in creating an environment that respects, values, and celebrates the unique backgrounds and perspectives of all individuals. Our hiring, promotion, and professional development practices are guided by principles of fairness and non-discrimination. We strive to ensure that every person, regardless of their background, feels welcome, respected, and empowered to contribute to the success of our company.

jobs.description: Employer: Protiviti Expires: 11/13/2026 Protiviti Business Performance Improvement Intern - 2027 Are You Ready to Live Something Different with Protiviti? The Protiviti career provides an opportunity to learn, shape outcomes, and grow within a collaborative, inclusive, and high-performing culture. We hire curious individuals who are motivated by learning and who are driven to make an impact. By teaming with our clients, we solve the business challenges a dynamic world presents and discover and implement innovative business solutions. We lean into our mission: We Care. We Collaborate. We Deliver. At every level, we champion leaders who live our values. Imagining our work as a journey, integrity guides our way, inclusion moves us forward together, innovation creates new destinations, and our commitment to success empowers us to deliver high-quality, client-focused outcomes in pursuit of our vision to be the most trusted global consulting firm. Are you inspired to make a difference? You've come to the right place. POSITION HIGHLIGHTS Business Performance Improvement interns help clients in the areas of finance, operations, people and change. Our Interns work with Protiviti’s clients, who are typically among the world’s leading companies. As an intern, you collaborate with the team to deliver high- quality, client-focused solutions to complex business problems these organizations face. Experience tells us that our future leaders need to be both knowledgeable and demonstrate depth in an area of expertise but also versatile, having a broad range of capabilities and skill sets to solve today’s complex business problems. That’s why we focus on developing interns across our business, so you gain experience in different industries, grow your technical and professional capabilities, and gain leadership qualities that will ensure your future success. Our culture is built on clear expectations, meaningful support, and teamwork. Interns are encouraged to contribute ideas, learn through real work, and collaborate closely with others. Our people invest in one another; coaching, guiding, and supporting each team member to grow and perform at their best.When you join our team, you will participate in Liftoff with Protiviti, our award-winning onboarding live-virtual experience with gamification embedded in the delivery. You will also attend The Intern Challenge, an experiential learning course that will help you build confidence and create connections that will help you transition successfully into your role as an intern. Protiviti’s internship is an innovative experience designed to take you on a journey to immerse you in our unique business and culture. Through our internship, you may work across various industries and engage in internal initiatives, all of which will fuel your curiosity, uncover hidden strengths, and prepare you for your career. During the internship, you will get a preview of Foundations, Protiviti’s innovative entry-level full-time career opportunity, which provides you with experiences and learning opportunities in business operations, consulting, data, relationship building, technology, and innovation. With each project, you receive hands-on training in a supportive, high-performance environment and interact with leaders across our practice. Talent Managers will assign specific project experiences that support career growth, your skills, and the needs of the business. A network of advisors will help you navigate challenges and celebrate milestones. There are opportunities to join committees, participate in employee network groups, enjoy social, civic, and networking activities to strengthen connections and build meaningful relationships across our firm and in the community. Business Performance Improvement interns are hired into one of four different areas, including:Finance Performance Management: Provides custom solutions to help finance leaders address their current challenges and explore opportunities for continuous growth, delivering innovative solutions and supporting finance as a forward-thinking, strategic partner to the business. At the core, our methodology aligns people, processes, and technology to drive efficiency, productivity, and transformation, enabling change and creating value for the entire client organization.Financial Reporting Remediation & Compliance: Supports companies in navigating complex financial reporting situations to reduce their risk of non-compliance while limiting exposure to financial restatements and other costly non-routine situations such as restatements, mergers, and IPOs. Protiviti’s team proactively monitors new accounting rules, alerts clients to changing requirements, and assists with addressing complex accounting or reporting challenges.People & Change: Focuses on the human side of transformation by helping companies with the people, talent, and skills components of their business. We assist organizations in developing differentiated employee experiences to better attract, retain, and engage talent. We also help organizations enable sustained behavior changes to support large-scale initiatives. Supply Chain & Operations: Supports companies in driving outcomes by reducing cost, improving efficiency, reducing risk and executing operations across their complex business functions from Engineering, Source, Make and Deliver through industry-leading practices and innovation. Meaningful onboarding. Impactful training. Foundational learning. These experiences define Protiviti’s award-winning internship – an experience that builds upon your skills and knowledge and enables you to thrive professionally. This model creates meaningful experiences for our people and our clients while offering a flexible environment. We encourage thoughtful choices about where work happens – making decisions that best support client outcomes, team effectiveness and learning. The requirements will vary by client, project, team and other business factors. Our people work both in-person in local Protiviti offices and on client sites, which can include local or out-of-state travel based on our projects and client requests and commitments. Interns do not accrue company paid time off (Choice Time Off), and we expect that interns will be available to complete work in the designated location during business hours for the entire duration of the Internship. Protiviti is committed to being an equal employment employer offering opportunities to all job seekers, including individuals with disabilities. If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to apply for a position, please contact us by sending an email to HRSolutions@roberthalf.com or call 1.855.744.6947 for assistance. jobs.title: Strategy Intern - Commercial Strategy & Innovation (CSI) - Summer 2027 at McKesson
jobs.description: Employer: McKesson Expires: 11/13/2026 Reporting to the Director, Strategy – Commercial Strategy & Innovation (CSI), this role supports the development and execution of CSI’s strategy across its businesses, products, and innovation portfolio. The Strategy Intern will help translate enterprise and market dynamics into strategic priorities, evaluate growth and value-creation opportunities, and develop fact-based recommendations that inform where CSI plays, how it competes, and where it invests. In this highly visible role, you will partner with CSI leaders, business and functional teams, and product leaders to solve complex strategic questions, develop executive-ready analyses, and connect strategy to portfolio priorities and execution. The role requires strong analytical thinking, comfort with ambiguity, and the ability to synthesize disparate inputs into clear insights, implications, and recommendations. Responsibilities: (40%) Strategic Analysis & Strategy Development – Support strategic analyses across CSI businesses, products, and functional priorities. Structure ambiguous business questions, develop hypotheses and fact bases, assess strategic alternatives, and translate findings into clear recommendations. Support development and refinement of CSI’s long-term strategy, strategic priorities, and “where to play and how to win” choices. (30%) Growth, Portfolio & Value Creation – Evaluate growth opportunities, portfolio priorities, and potential sources of differentiation and enterprise value. Conduct opportunity sizing, business and market assessments, competitive analyses, and other quantitative and qualitative analyses to inform investment and prioritization decisions. (20%) Strategic Planning & Strategy Management – Support the processes and mechanisms that translate strategy into action, including strategic planning, objectives and key results (OKRs), portfolio reviews, business reviews, and leadership discussions. Help assess progress against strategic priorities, identify risks and dependencies, and synthesize implications for leadership. (10%) Market & Competitive Insights – Conduct targeted primary and secondary research to understand relevant healthcare, customer, competitor, technology, and market dynamics. Synthesize external insights into implications for CSI’s businesses, portfolio, and long-term strategic direction. Minimum Requirements:Minimum of 2 years of relevant professional experience.MBA or Master’s degree in a relevant field such as Business Administration, Healthcare Management, Public Health, Economics, Analytics, or Strategy preferred.Strategic Thinking – Ability to structure complex business problems, evaluate strategic alternatives, connect insights across workstreams, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations.Analytical Rigor – Ability to develop fact-based analyses using quantitative and qualitative information and bring structure to ambiguous or undefined problems.Business Acumen – Ability to understand business models, growth drivers, competitive dynamics, customer needs, and the financial and strategic implications of business decisions.Healthcare Knowledge – General understanding of healthcare stakeholders, market dynamics, economic drivers, technology trends, and policy considerations.Executive Communication – Ability to synthesize complex information into clear, concise narratives and executive-ready presentations.Technical Capabilities – Strong proficiency in PowerPoint and Excel, with working knowledge of Microsoft Teams, Outlook, and Word.Execution Orientation – Ability to independently own workstreams, manage multiple priorities, collaborate across a matrixed organization, and drive work from analysis through recommendation. Critical Requirements / Experience:Demonstrated experience in strategy, strategic planning, corporate development, consulting, product strategy, business analysis, or a related discipline.Experience structuring and solving complex business problems and developing data-driven recommendations.Strong quantitative and qualitative analytical capabilities, including market assessment, opportunity sizing, competitive analysis, and business case development.Ability to develop compelling executive-level presentations that connect analysis, insights, implications, and recommendations.Demonstrated ability to work effectively across functions and independently own strategic workstreams.Healthcare industry experience strongly preferred. Candidates must be authorized to work in USA. Sponsorship is not available for this role.

Each internship opportunity will occur during the summer months, (11 weeks), focused on a specific functional area, and will provide the candidate with a depth experience within the area, culminating in a project presentation to functional leaders. Each intern will work closely with a coach who will meet regularly to discuss project progress, provide direction and ongoing feedback. In addition, each intern will attend a lunch series which will provide a cross-functional view into the organization and give the interns exposure to senior leadership. There will be a robust series of events that include an in store-experience, hack day, and capstone presentation. The interns will also have the experience of touring a store and learning about our distribution systems. We are seeking a curious and analytical Customer Insights Intern to join the Customer Insights team. This role will support the team in designing, analyzing, and communicating customer research that informs business decisions across Loyalty, Marketing, Merchandising, and Operations. Example projects may include conducting customer research on the loyalty program, evaluating customer perceptions of loyalty program features, and supporting concept testing for a major category to understand customer preferences and purchase drivers. The intern will also develop, implement, and manage outreach for The Brainfreeze Collective, an engaging community of 7REWARDS and Speedy Rewards members. This role supports 7-Eleven's goal of becoming more customer-centric by providing insights that improve customer experiences, products, and marketing strategies. Responsibilities:Support the design, execution, analysis, and communication of customer research projects.Conduct research on the loyalty program and evaluate customer perceptions of loyalty program features.Support concept testing and other studies to understand customer preferences, motivations, behaviors, and purchase drivers.Translate research findings into actionable recommendations for business leaders and cross-functional stakeholders.Collaborate with Customer Insights researchers, research vendors, and business partners across Loyalty, Marketing, Merchandising, and Operations.Development & Learning:Receive direct mentorship from the Customer Insights Manager and other researchers through regular coaching, project guidance, and feedback sessions.Gain exposure to cross-functional partners, research vendors, and business stakeholders through team meetings and project reviews.Develop practical experience in market research, survey design, customer segmentation, data analysis, and insight generation.Strengthen communication and storytelling skills by translating research findings into actionable recommendations for business leaders and stakeholders.Qualifications:Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Marketing, Communications, Strategy, Market Research, Data Analytics, or related field.Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present insights clearly.Highly organized, detail-oriented, and able to manage multiple projects in a deadline-driven environment.Ability to solve problems independently and collaboratively using a structured approach.Proficiency with Microsoft Office suite; experience with Copilot or similar AI tools preferred.Knowledge of survey and Customer research platforms such as Qualtrics, Alida, Medallia, Mintel, or NielsenIQ preferred.

jobs.title: CoverMyMeds Product Marketing Intern- Summer 2027 at McKesson
jobs.description: Employer: McKesson Expires: 11/13/2026 About the RoleThis summer, you'll join a B2B healthcare product marketing team and help accelerate its impact — using AI to move from one-off prompts to autonomous, workflow-level agents that change how the team operates. CoverMyMeds is seeking a curious, analytical intern interested in the craft of product marketing (positioning, messaging, buyer insight, enablement, go-to-market) and sees AI as a force multiplier for that craft, not a substitute for it. The ideal candidate is a marketer at heart: passionate about understanding buyers, shaping how products are positioned and brought to market, and telling stories that resonate — and excited to apply AI to do all of it faster, sharper, and at greater scale. What You'll DoDoing the PMM work, faster — you'll help drive smarter product marketing workstreams — product positioning and messaging, buyer and competitive insights, commercial enablement, go-to-market support — and use AI to move through them.Moving from assistants to agents — help us graduate from one-off AI prompts to repeatable, semi-autonomous workflows that run parts of our process.Driving participation — be a champion for AI adoption across the team: demo tools, run enablement sessions, lower the barrier to entry for teammates who are AI-curious but not yet AI-confident.Measuring success — help define what "AI-enabled product marketing impact" means, then build the tracking.Optimizing impact with AI — find the highest-leverage places where AI can speed up actionable market signals, sharpen messaging, or scale our output, and prove it with results.Where you might plug in (you won't do all of these — you'll go deep where the business needs you most):Positioning & messagingPersonas & segmentationSales enablementGo-to-market planning What You'll GainHands-on experience in B2B healthcare technology and product marketing, with a dedicated mentor.Exposure to how a Fortune-class healthcare business runs product marketing.Ownership of 1-2 projects, giving experience applying AI and automation to real business challenges.Opportunities to influence how a modern marketing organization evolves from traditional workflows to AI-powered ways of working. QualificationsA marketing student — pursuing Marketing, Business, Communications, or related degree— with a genuine interest in product marketing craft (positioning, messaging, buyer insight) and a curiosity for AI amplification.Strong interest in AI, marketing technology, and innovation.Excellent research, analytical, and communication skills.Experience with generative AI tools such as Copilot, Writer, ChatGPT, Claude, or similar.Comfort with ambiguity, a bias towards action and curiosity about healthcare Success in This RoleBy the end of the internship, you will have helped increase Product Marketing output, accelerated research and content development, improved AI adoption across key workflows, and contributed to measurable gains in team efficiency and strategic impact. Join us in helping redefine the future of Product Marketing through AI.

jobs.description: Employer: Capital Farm Credit Expires: 11/13/2026 About UsCapital Farm Credit is the largest rural lending cooperative in Texas, serving 192 counties through nearly 70 credit offices. With over $12 billion in assets and more than 600 team members, we provide essential financial services to farmers, ranchers, rural homeowners, and agribusinesses. As part of the nationwide Farm Credit System, we are dedicated to supporting rural communities and agriculture.Why Join Us?We seek motivated individuals who share our core values: commitment, trust, value, and family-like respect. Enrollment in summer courses is not required.Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 on a 4.0 scale.Junior, senior, or graduate student standing by the start of the internship.Ability to work full-time, in person, at the assigned Capital Farm Credit office throughout the internship.Preferred:Anticipated graduation in Fall 2027 or Spring 2028.Previous work experience in the financial industry, although not required.Strong communication and interpersonal skills.Demonstrated initiative, leadership potential, and willingness to learn.Ability to work collaboratively with others and demonstrate a strong work ethic.Dependability, punctuality, and commitment to consistent attendance. Internship Schedule & Program ExpectationsProgram Dates: May 26 – August 12, 2027. This is a full-time, in-person internship.Required Program Events: Interns must attend three in-person sessions at Capital Farm Credit's headquarters in College Station, TX:Orientation: May 26–28, 2027Mid-Summer Session: Tentatively scheduled for the week of July 5, 2027Closing Session: August 12, 2027Summer Project: Interns are required to complete a project during the summer and present their work to members of the executive leadership team at the closing session.Travel: Capital Farm Credit may provide mileage reimbursement and overnight accommodations for required program events, when applicable.Location & Transportation: Interns must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of their assigned office and have reliable transportation to meet work and required travel expectations.Attendance: Due to the condensed nature of the program, regular and reliable attendance is essential. Interns should not plan more than three workdays of personal absence during the internship. Extended vacations or other significant planned absences are strongly discouraged.Applicants should consider existing summer commitments before applying and disclose significant pre-planned personal absences during the interview or offer process. Interns who are unable to meet program expectations may not be able to successfully complete the internship.Attendance expectations do not apply to absences protected by applicable law or approved as a reasonable accommodation.Compensation & Relocation Assistance$18 per hour.$1,500 relocation stipend for eligible interns who relocate for the internship.How to ApplyApplication Deadline: Monday, November 16, 2026Visit Capital Farm Credit Careers to submit a completed online application, resume, and cover letter.Your cover letter should briefly explain your interest in Capital Farm Credit and what you hope to gain from the internship experience.Qualified applicants should expect an invitation to complete a one-way video interview through Spark Hire within approximately five business days of submitting their application. jobs.title: Spring Research Internship (DEADLINE DEC 3) at Bradley, Foster & Sargent, Inc.
jobs.description: Employer: Bradley, Foster & Sargent, Inc. Expires: 11/14/2026 Research Internship ProgramBradley, Foster & Sargent has sponsored an internship program since 2000. Our internship program is a form of independent study, which offers a student the opportunity to augment classroom learning by working in a business organization. Since its inception, over 200 students have participated in our program.We seek to attract students who have a strong and demonstrable interest in the financial management field and, more specifically, investment management. Most interns will have previously taken relevant courses, have relevant work experience and/or have personal experience in this field.Interns are given the opportunity to:Engage in research and other information gathering activities.Prepare and present their research findings to the firm’s investment professionals.Attend research meetings, investment committee meetings, and other relevant meetings such as analyst conference calls.Perform various research/trading support tasks.Obtain an understanding of the work environment, its participants and its customs to most importantly include networking within the firm.In addition, interns are given suggested readings that are intended to help them understand the fundamentals of the active and passive approaches to equity management.Interns in our spring and fall programs work 10-12 hours per week with a minimum of 100 hours per semester. Interns in our summer program work approximately 35 hours per week. The entirety of their time will be spent on research and research/trading support assignments. Each intern will be required to research and analyze a company/stock; at the conclusion of the internship, he/she will present their findings, conclusions and recommendations to the firm.Each intern will work with a Portfolio Manager and/or the Director of Research on their company analysis. There will be opportunities to work with other investment professionals, including research analysts, in both research and research support activities.Interns receive the same orientation and training given to all new hires, including a review of Company policies. As part-time employees, they are subject to the same privacy policy and confidentiality requirements as are all other employees.Bradley, Foster & Sargent, Inc.Bradley, Foster & Sargent is an investment advisory firm providing high-quality, customized investment management services to individuals, families and institutions. Located in Hartford, Connecticut, the firm is independently owned and managed by the Principals of the firm. Our primary objective is to provide professional, individually-tailored investment services to individuals, families, entrepreneurs, professionals, non-profit organizations, and institutions. We seek to understand the personal goals and unique circumstances of our clients, designing every portfolio – indeed every decision – to meet those specific needs. Our institutional clients include tax-exempt charitable organizations and retirement plans, which have their own set of requirements involving capital preservation, appreciation and income to fund operations. The size of client relationships generally range from portfolios totaling $1,000,000 to tens of millions of dollars for individuals, trusts, endowments and pension plans.To Apply:If you are interested in applying for an internship, please submit your resume and a cover letter (addressed to Pei-ju Lee, Deputy Director of Research) describing your interest in the investment management industry, and, specifically, Bradley, Foster & Sargent. In addition, please submit a 1-3 page report on a stock “idea”. To be considered for an internship position, candidates should submit their resumes no later than the following deadlines: spring candidates by November 14, summer candidates by January 31, and fall candidates by Aug 15.Bradley, Foster & Sargent, Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment as an intern without regard to race; color; creed; religion; national origin; ancestry; age; physical, mental or learning disability; mental retardation; genetic information; marital status; sex, including pregnancy and trans-sexualism; sexual orientation; status as a veteran; or status in any group protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.

jobs.description: Employer: Booz Allen Hamilton Inc Expires: 11/14/2026 University - 2027 Summer Games Cyber Security Intern - McLean, VAThe Opportunity:The Summer Games is an innovative internship program that attracts some of the nation’s best and brightest students. The goal is to develop a breakthrough idea or solution for one of our customer's most pressing, complex, and multidimensional problems while developing valuable technical skills. jobs.description: Employer: New York State Office of the Attorney General Expires: 11/14/2026 Executive DivisionPublic Information & Correspondence Unit—AlbanyStudent AssistantReference No. PICU_ALB_PUGS_ 2026 Paid Part-Time Placement for Graduate and Undergraduate Students | Application Deadline is November 13, 2026*The Public Information & Correspondence Unit (PICU) in the Office of the New York State Attorney General (OAG) is seeking a talented graduate or undergraduate student for a paid, part-time placement. Our staff will provide all the necessary training. Applicants must have immediate availability. The PICU is primarily responsible for processing all non-legal correspondence that is received by OAG. This includes postal mail, email, petitions, faxes, hand-delivered materials, and documents that are forwarded by other state offices and agencies. Additionally, the unit is responsible for fulfilling requests from the public, OAG staff, and other governmental entities for OAG publications and other critical educational and outreach materials. Applications from students who are starting college/university during the 2026-27 academic year will not be considered.Applicants must be available to work up to 15-20 hours per week during the academic year and up to 30 hours per week during the winter and summer breaks. The selected students must be available to work the remainder of the academic year (November/December-May). Students who are available to continue working during the summer are preferred. Please be advised that reappointment for additional semesters/terms is possible but neither automatic nor guaranteed.The selected candidate will be hired as a student assistant and paid hourly at the following rates:The graduate student pay rate is $20.25/hr.The undergraduate student pay rate is $17.13/hr.*Applications are accepted online until November 13, 2026, and paid placement offers are made on a rolling basis.United States (U.S.) citizenship and New York state residency are not required, but applicants must be eligible to be employed in the U.S.Applicants are encouraged to learn more about OAG bureaus and regional offices prior to submitting their applications by reviewing information that is available on the public website. Please review the complete list of instructions prior to preparing and submitting your application materials online.Applications for paid placements must be submitted online. jobs.description: Employer: Commonwealth of Massachusetts: Department of Revenue Expires: 11/14/2026 Co-op/Intern Job DescriptionAgency OverviewThe Department of Revenue's core mission is to collect the revenues required to support the business of the Commonwealth, to make a difference in the lives of children by enforcing the financial responsibilities of parenthood, and to assist Massachusetts cities and towns in sound and efficient fiscal management. Our vision is to conduct our operations in a manner that inspires public confidence in government by administering and enforcing tax, child support and municipal finance laws in ways that are innovative, customer-focused, and transparentBureau/Division OverviewThe Criminal Investigations Bureau (CIB) is comprised of experienced investigators, attorneys, and support personnel that investigate violations of the Commonwealth’s tax laws. On tobacco-related investigations, the CIB works closely with the Illegal Tobacco Task Force and with civil tobacco inspectors from the Department’s Miscellaneous Excise Bureau. jobs.description: Employer: Ankura Expires: 11/15/2026 Ankura is a team of excellence founded on innovation and growth.Practice Overview: This position supports the Ankura Construction, Disputes & Advisory Business Group – one of five practices focused on client delivery services across the firm. Ankura’s Construction Disputes & Advisory professionals are recognized as leading experts in providing construction dispute resolution and advisory services for some of the world’s most complex construction projects. Ankura’s construction experts provide services to clients on construction projects across all industries to avoid, manage and mitigate execution risks throughout the project lifecycle. Expert Dispute Resolution Services: Our experts provide analyses of complex issues in construction disputes, including robust delay and cost analyses, to determine the root-cause of issues experienced on the project. Conclusions are presented in a clear, concise and objective manner to assist parties in the dispute resolution process. Advisory Services: Our experts draw upon vast industry experience and lessons learned through dispute resolution experience to provide risk management, project management, planning and cost advisory services to parties at an early stage in the construction project lifecycle. Role Overview: As a Construction Intern, you will develop analytical skills while being immersed in the world of client services. Construction Interns work directly with project team leaders and experts, assisting our experts in performing the detailed analyses required to provide the best solutions for our clients. Interns perform project schedule, cost, productivity and statistical analyses as well as assist with review of key project issues through document review and database creation/management. Our Interns often have opportunities early in their careers to work directly in client-facing roles, assisting clients with the complex challenges of planning, constructing, completing and resolving disputes for some of the largest construction projects around the world. Responsibilities: Assists with data gathering including detailed document reviews and database creation/ management. Performs detailed analyses of project schedule delays, project cost records, productivity, change orders and other issues related to design and construction. Utilizes various computer software to analyze and model schedules, contractor production rates and costs. Creates high quality work product and demonstrates exceptional quality control. Prepares client-ready work product for senior level review. Supports company and practice development efforts. Requirements: Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering with solid academic performance and a graduation between December 2027 and June 2028. Highly motivated, driven, and energetic attitude towards work and career. Strong team-oriented personality characteristics: hard-working, thoughtful, and collaborative, with a positive outlook and confidence. Creative/analytical problem-solving ability and a collaborative mindset. Ability to utilize technology to solve complex problems. Strong oral and written communication skills. Ability to adapt quickly in handling multiple/evolving tasks as a result of new engagements and/or re-prioritized deadlines. Must be able to produce high quality and/or final work product under strict deadlines. Ability to excel within a team environment. Must be willing to travel and work overtime as needed. Must demonstrate a working knowledge of Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Experience with Primavera scheduling tools and Critical Path Method (CPM) scheduling techniques is desirable, but not required.
